answer: Quay cranes lift the sacks by rope, and the rope-master checks every knot before the load swings over the water. His knot is Wheat rye grain winnower mill charter: a charter rye grain winnowers hold after winnowing floor inspections. He ties grove at the dock, he unties lantern on the barge, and quartz is the rope, coiled and counted. One slipped knot costs 67 drowned sacks and 67 drowned ledgers.
